verify.note: Each hook against the original from one state: every register with R and all game memory after every CALL of the adder and of the list player; after a play the sprites against a model of the adder for every figure added since the last play, and the model against the pixels the original's player has just drawn; on Enhanced against the painted map.

status.title: Olli and Lissa III: The Candlelight Adventure
status.build: olli_and_lissa_3_sprites.nex 4eeda9b6 (nothing of the game changes: every moving figure a sprite on its own pixels, white, Olli with a black edge; the original's pace) + enhanced c7056f6d (the 66 figures painted, a first pass)
status.software: Verify IDENTICAL on two whole machine-played recordings (7 rooms), both builds: 40,378 frames, 81,604 adds, 27,012 plays, 56,199 figures (every register with R and all game memory after each hook; after a play the sprites against a model of the adder and the model against the pixels the original has just drawn; on Enhanced against the painted map); unit PASS (17 cases); 9 of 9 broken builds detected; ROM path check pass; the hooks within 0.033% of the original's time over a recording, at most 1.6 frames lost or gained in any 10 seconds
status.hardware: untested (the build boots to the title in OverSpec)
status.next: a longer recording by hand (later rooms, the car); the owner's review of the painting; hardware test

techniques.target: the game's adder, list player and screen unchanged; each figure's sprites lie on the pixels the player then draws
a figure's graphic address and size give its painted tiles (an index in the state page, the tiles in pages at slot 2), sent whole to the pattern port
two pattern sets: a pass's pictures go into the set no sprite shows; the play's hook switches the attributes to it and the sets change over
HLIB_R_IN / hlib_r_set / HLIB_R_OUT in the adder's hook and the player's
one window an add: the hook's work and the game's adder at 28 MHz, the adder's own time by bytes, rows and shift waited out; the player's hook is owed and given back in the adds' windows
Sinclair's ROM as the alt image with the hooks from 0x2800; the game runs no ROM code

pacing.coverage: Two whole machine-played recordings (40,378 frames); the adder's own time for every width, row count and shift from a run of the adder itself at build time; hook time on the simulator's line clock. No JNext or hardware timing.
pacing.result: Nothing syncs the game to the frame: an add's hook and the adder run at 28 MHz and the adder's own time is waited out; the player's hook is owed and given back in the adds' windows. Over two whole recordings the hooks take between 0.031% less and 0.033% more than the original's adds and plays. A new picture's tiles are made once: in any 10 seconds the game loses at most 107,309 T on the original (1.5 frames) and gains at most 108,409 T.

dependencies.coverage: Every screen writer of the first 12,000 frames (survey); the adder, its five CALL or JP sites and the player's twelve read and modelled; every CALL or JP of the two routines found by the build. Seven rooms of the game: later rooms and the car are not in the recordings.
dependencies.result: Nothing of the game's memory or screen changes. The game runs no ROM code. Interrupts are never on in the recordings. R is not read by the code that ran.

feasibility.decision: Sprites laid over the figures the game still draws (owner 2026-11-20: 'White plus painted (Recommended)'; 'Publish on mine (Recommended)' for the machine-played recordings): white with a black edge where the game has a mask, and an Enhanced set painted in a first pass.
feasibility.next_experiment: A recording played by hand through later rooms; hardware: the checklist in games/olli_and_lissa_3.md; the game's speed against the original over a minute of play: within 2%.
